summary: The battery-electric CLA sedan is the first car on Mercedes-Benz's MMA platform and, alongside the run-out EQA, the brand's entry point into electric motoring here, sold in two grades (the CLA Shooting Brake wagon is a separate body). Australian reviewers are near-unanimous that the efficiency and charging hardware are class-leading — an 800-volt system, 320kW DC peak and a 663km WLTP claim on the dual-motor grade — but split on the drive: CarExpert found it soft and 'a bit ordinary', Chasing Cars praised a polished ride and well-balanced handling, and both note the fastback roofline costs rear-seat headroom. It reads as a car chosen for range, charging speed and efficiency rather than driver engagement.
pros: The 350 4MATIC claims 663km WLTP, comfortably ahead of the BMW i4 eDrive35's 448km at similar money
800-volt architecture peaks at 320kW DC, enough to add roughly 300km in about ten minutes — nothing else near this price charges as fast

The CLA 200 at $72,200 sits under the $75,000 cap that keeps the full FBT exemption from 1 April 2027; the 350 4MATIC at $91,300 clears the $91,661 LCT threshold by just $361 but loses the full exemption then
Real-world efficiency matches the claims: Chasing Cars measured 13.4kWh/100km in the CLA 200 and 14.3kWh/100km in the 350 4MATIC, and CarExpert rated the ride 'almost pillow-like'
A 101-litre front boot supplements the 405-litre rear boot, and both grades are rated to tow braked (1500kg and 1800kg)
cons: Rear headroom is tight for anyone over 1.8m and the high battery floor leaves thighs unsupported — the four-door-coupe roofline costs real space
CarExpert's verdict is that it is 'a bit ordinary to drive', with muted steering feel and early understeer even in the 260kW 350 4MATIC
The 800-volt-only design cannot use older 400V-limited DC chargers, including many Australian 50kW units, without the factory DC-DC converter
Mercedes EV resale in Australia has been weak: the EQA and EQB needed repeated local price cuts, and run-out EQA stock is discounted well below list
Almost every physical control has gone, with MB.OS moving climate and drive functions onto the touchscreens
